items.title: VisionQuest: What You Need to Remember Before the New MCU Show
items.excerpt: Here's everything you need to know about the Vision, Wanda, Tommy and Billy, and much more before watching the latest MCU show, VisionQuest.
items.content_text: Marvel Studios and Disney+ are about to debut their newest MCU series, VisionQuest , which seems like a good time to look back at Vision’s quest so far. In the new series, which is described as the conclusion of a trilogy that also includes WandaVision and Agatha All Along , Vision is spending time inside a virtual world, where he is in contact with AI personas we’ve met before in the MCU, most notably the dreaded Ultron. And at the same time, in the real world, Vision comes into contact with a teenager who’s the reincarnation of one of his sons, Tommy. It’s been a wild journey for the Vision and those he’s closest to, filled with birth, death, rebirth, and sitcom recreations. So let’s look back at the story so far for Vision, Ultron, Tommy and other VisionQuest characters - and potential characters. You can watch the full video above, or read the full story below... or just jump to the parts you're most interested in! In the Beginning, There Was JARVIS JARVIS was a powerful AI system created by Tony Stark to assist him in his work. The persona for the witty, British accented JARVIS was modeled after Edwin Jarvis, who served as the butler to Tony’s father, Howard Stark, for decades, clearly making an impact on young Tony in the process. After Tony became Iron Man, JARVIS was a crucial part of testing and controlling the many iterations of the Iron Man suit. JARVIS would eventually also run Tony’s Iron Legion robotic army and be of service to the Avengers at large after Tony helped found that team. And Then Came Ultron Tony and his fellow Avenger Bruce Banner began to develop the idea for Ultron, intended as an incredibly advanced AI system that could combine with the Iron Legion to form a formidable global peacekeeping force, and believed the complex neural network found within the scepter once wielded by Loki could be the key to Ultron’s creation. Upon awakening though, Ultron immediately had his own ideas on how to proceed, believing humanity was their own worst enemy and should be destroyed. Ultron seemingly destroyed JARVIS to stop him from hindering his plans, before inhabiting the first of many robot forms. Ultron would recruit superpowered twins Wanda and Pietro Maximoff to help him, who already had a vendetta against Tony Stark because their parents were killed by a Stark-built missile. But even as Ultron was putting his consciousness into ever more powerful robotic bodies, he wanted something more permanent. He used the object that had actually been powering Loki’s scepter the entire time, the Infinity Stone known as the Mind Stone, as a crucial element to power a new synthetic body that utilized the nearly indestructible, Wakandan-honed substance known as Vibranium. The Birth of Vision The Avengers managed to capture Ultron’s intended new body before he could finish uploading his consciousness to it, assisted by Wanda and Pietro, who had come to realize their new pal’s genocidal intent. Tony discovered JARVIS had in fact survived, hiding from Ultron while working to stop him from gaining control of nuclear weapons systems. Tony decided to reconfigure JARVIS’ matrix and place it within the very body Ultron wanted for himself, which Thor ended up giving the final power boost to, creating an android, or Synthezoid to use the proper Marvel vernacular, who came to be known as the Vision. And while he retained JARVIS’ speaking voice, and desire to protect humanity, he considered himself as something new entirely. Along with Wanda and Pietro, Vision teamed with the Avengers to face off with Ultron in Wanda and Pietro’s home country of Sokovia. His formidable abilities, including super strength, flight, intangibility, and a beam he could shoot from the Mind Stone, all helped him make an impact, as did the fact that he’s one of the very few beings who could actually lift Thor’s hammer. (Though whether this is because he is a living being deemed worthy or an artificial being outside of the parameters of the hammer’s enchantment remains up for debate.) After all of Ultron’s robot sentries were destroyed, Vision then faced his robotic “father” of sorts, stopping Ultron from escaping by destroying his final body. Wanda and Vision With several of the original Avengers departing at this point, Vision was then recruited for a new incarnation of the team, alongside Captain America, Black Widow, War Machine, the Falcon, and Wanda - the latter of whom had just lost Pietro in the fight against Ultron. In their time together as Avengers, an unlikely but palatable spark between Wanda and Vision grew, as he helped her process her brother’s death, complete with one hell of a great observation: “What is grief if not love enduring?” After Wanda accidentally caused the death of innocents in the midst of a mission, the announcement that the United Nations were planning to ratify the Sokovia Accords caused a huge rift within the Avengers, who split over those who sided with the Accords’ intention of an outside group having oversight over the team vs. those who worried it could hinder them or be used for nefarious purposes. While Wanda was, like Steve Rogers, ultimately firmly against the Accords, Vision backed Tony Stark’s support for them, believing that the existence of the Avengers and superheroes in general were causing new, more dangerous threats to rise against them. While Vision fought with Iron Man’s forces, Wanda ended up joining Captain America’s rogue group. Attempts to not actually cause lasting harm to those who were mostly friends and allies on the other side failed though, with Vision rushing to a wounded Wanda’s side only to inadvertently badly injure War Machine, who was permanently disabled as a result. After Cap’s group, Wanda included, went on the run as fugitives, Vision and Wanda couldn’t resist their strong connection, periodically sneaking away for what turned into a romantic relationship, during which they lived as normal a life as they could, as he masked his true form to the public. Thanos and the Death of Vision But their peace was interrupted by Thanos and his forces, who were now on the war path in an attempt to gather every Infinity Stone, including the one that sat within Vision’s forehead. As attempts to remove the Stone from him while keeping him alive ran out of time, and realizing the cataclysmic consequences if Thanos were to succeed in getting all the Stones, Vision asked Wanda to destroy the Mind Stone, despite knowing that it would kill him. Though in anguish over it, she agreed and took his life, only for Thanos to make an awful situation much worse. He used the Time Stone to reverse the last few moments, bringing Vision back to life just so he could tear the Mind Stone from his head, killing Vision once again in front of a distraught Wanda. Thanos then used the combined Infinity Stones to complete his plan to eliminate half of all life in the universe, with Wanda among those killed by the dreaded snap. Five years later, the remaining Avengers managed to reassemble the Stones and bring back everyone who the snap had killed, including a vengeful Wanda, but that didn’t help the Vision, who’d been killed in a different manner. WandaVision After Thanos’ defeat, Wanda, who had returned to life having skipped over those five years, and still feeling the raw loss of Vision, discovered his body had been dismantled and analyzed by the organization SWORD, who had tried to resurrect him without success. Overwhelmed with grief, the increasingly powerful Wanda – whose natural affinity for magic had been amplified by Hydra’s experiments on her – retreated into an idyllic world of her own creation, conjuring a massive magical hex that transformed the New Jersey suburb of Westview. Using the American sitcoms she grew up watching as inspiration, she put all of Westview’s residents into an ever-evolving TV scenario, where she lived as the newly married wife of her great love, the Vision - who was in fact a replica created by Wanda herself. Tommy and Billy Going even further, Wanda used her magic to cause herself to get pregnant and rapidly give birth to twin sons for her and Vision, Tommy and Billy, who continued to age years in a moment. However, the version of Vision she created was so true to the original that he began to realize something was wrong with Westview and its entranced populace. Eventually, despite Wanda continually resetting things to try and keep him oblivious, he was horrified to discover the dark nature of what Wanda had done, even as it also became clear that Vision and the twins could not physically exist outside the hex they were a part of. The White Vision With the government aware of the bizarre situation inside Westview, SWORD sent a weapon to kill Wanda in the form of the original Vision, rebuilt and finally reactivated thanks to SWORD using Wanda’s own magic to do so. Crucially, he was blocked off from his memories and the attached emotions of all he had experienced, including his love of Wanda, acting cold and genuinely robotic in a way he never had before. The hex-created Vision leapt to Wanda’s defense, with the two Visions initially having a furious fight. However, the Hex Vision was finally able to reason with the original Vision, convincing him to let him unlock the memories of the life he’d forgotten as an Avenger and his time with Wanda. Overwhelmed, he flew off to parts unknown… and his own series we’re finally about to get five years later! Rise of the Scarlet Witch Meanwhile, in the midst of a confrontation with the centuries old witch Agatha Harkness, who was attempting to take Wanda’s powers for herself, Wanda unlocked her full potential as the long prophesied Scarlet Witch, said to have a mastery of chaos magic above all others. After defeating Agatha, she finally decided to free the town from her thrall, even though ending the hex also meant the end of the lives she’d created inside it that she loved so much, the replica Vision and Tommy and Billy. But the replica Vision, glad she was doing the right thing, and recalling all the incarnations of both Jarvis and the Vision so far, told her he felt that somehow they’d be reunited. However, in the aftermath of yet another massive loss, Wanda proved unable to accept the absence of her children. Her ensuing attempt to steal counterparts of Tommy and Billy from a powerless version of herself in another part of the multiverse would ultimately lead to more regret and to Wanda sacrificing herself in order to destroy the source of the dark magic she had used. Agatha Harkness and Billy But what Wanda didn’t realize was that her Tommy and Billy actually still existed, because as it turned out, as the hex fell, Billy – who’d inherited both his mother’s telepathy and magical abilities – was able to pull his and his brother’s souls from their bodies. Billy sent his own soul into the body of a 13 year old boy who was simultaneously dying in a car crash. Now living that boy’s life, as William Kaplan, a confused Billy couldn’t recall his real history, but investigating the events of the Westview anomaly, gradually came to realize who he was in the years that followed. Billy was determined to find Tommy, and with the help of an unlikely ally, in the form of Agatha Harkness, he was able to pinpoint Tommy’s still adrift soul and place it into the body of an ostracized boy who had just drowned thanks to a cruel prank, though Billy couldn’t perceive the specifics on where this took place. When Death herself came to claim Billy, whose resurrection had defied her will, Agatha – having come to truly care for Billy – sacrificed herself instead. However, resisting being pulled into the afterlife, Agatha continued on as a ghost, now accompanying Billy on the mission that mattered most to him. Next Up: VisionQuest Will Billy and Agatha be successful anytime soon? That remains to be seen, as they haven’t been announced as being in VisionQuest, but considering Tommy is definitely in that show, it certainly seems possible we might get an appearance. Regardless, we’ll find out what exactly both Billy’s brother, Tommy, and their father, The Vision, have been up to when VisionQuest debuts on Disney+.

items.title: Peak Has Been Leaked for PS5 by the ESRB
items.excerpt: The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak, has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB.
items.content_text: The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak , has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB. Last year, an adorable, cheap co-op game known as Peak blew up on Steam . In the game, players unite with their friends to pass through a wide variety of deadly obstacles in order to climb absurdly tall mountains. They must use the power of friendship and a handful of tools to overcome the odds, often resulting in hilarious deaths, injuries, and hijinks. As of August 2025, Peak has sold over 10 million copies , partially thanks to the fact it only costs $8 and is an easy sell to a group of friends. It seems like the game will likely only continue to grow its audience, as the ESRB has rated Peak for PS5. Historically, ESRB leaks are incredibly accurate, so it seems like only a matter of time before an official announcement is made. As of right now, it's unclear if Peak will also come to Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2, but it would be surprising if this remained console exclusive to PS5. Unfortunately for new players, Peak ended its post-launch support earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't expect the game to receive any significant content after it releases on console. It's also unclear if it will enjoy the same exceptionally low price when it does hit consoles, but it would be surprising if the team behind the game changed it. Following the game's release, the team noted that there's a psychology behind pricing a game that low . “We had this joke of, like, 'How much is a game really?'" said Peak co-creator Nick Kaman. "In a player’s mind, what does it mean to spend five bucks? Well, that’s five bucks. But six bucks? Well, that’s still five bucks. Four bucks is also kind of five bucks. Three bucks is two bucks. And two bucks is basically free. So we’ve got these tiers: You know, twelve bucks… that’s ten bucks. But thirteen bucks is fifteen bucks. And we found that eight bucks is still five bucks. It doesn’t become ten bucks. Seven ninety nine, that’s five bucks, right? So, eight bucks going to five bucks is the biggest differential we could find in pricing, so we found it very optimal.” It's unclear when an official announcement might follow, but if there's an ESRB rating, it typically means that the game isn't too far away from a release.

items.title: Save 20% Off the New Steelseries Aeon Pro Wireless Gaming Controller With Infinite Battery Life
items.excerpt: This controller is shaping up to be one of the best wireless PC and Xbox gaming controllers on the market.
items.content_text: SteelSeries recently released its new Aeon Pro wireless gaming controller for PC and Xbox and it's available to purchase at the Steelseries store for $209.99 after 20% off coupon code " SSPOUT20 ". At that price we'd be asking a lot from our controller, including top-tier build quality and a plethora of features, maybe even some unique to this controller. Fortunately, the Aeon Pro delivers. 20% Off the New SteelSeries Aeon Pro Gaming Controller SteelSeries already has a lineup of gaming controllers that includes the Stratus and Nimbus. The Aeon Pro, however, is the company's first high-end pro-grade controller. Honestly, it's shaping up to be one of the best PC and Xbox controllers ever. IGN's Bo Moore has already posted his Aeon Pro review-so-far and his initial impressions have been stellar. Wireless freedom with zero downtime Amongst the bevy of features packed in the Aeon Pro, one stands out in particular, and that's the infinite battery system. This is essentially a hot-swappable battery system much like what you'll find in the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro and Omni headsets, which I consider to be one of the best gaming headets on the market for this reason. The Aeon Pro basically includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your controller and the other to remain charged and ready to go in the docking station that doubles as a charger. You get wireless freedom with zero downtime . "Quick switch" between Xbox and PC The Aeon Pro's other standout feature is its patented QuickSwitch system. You can switch between Xbox, PC, or mobile instantly and seamlessly, with no re-pairing or re-plugging required. How does that even work? It's pretty simple, actually. In addition to being a charger for your batteries, the docking station is also a hub of sorts. You plug your Xbox and PC via USB Type-C ports on the rear, and the controller then connects wirelessly to the dock. For mobile, the connection is made via Bluetooth. Again, I've seen this technology before in the Arctis Nova Pro Omni headset, and SteelSeries carried this feature over to the Aeon Pro. That's a big brain move. Hall effect and micro-switches throughout My favorite gaming controllers in the past have two features they all have in common: Hall Effect joysticks and mechanical switches for nearly all of its buttons (including the d-pad). The Aeon Pro does not disappoint. Both joysticks use Hall Effect magnetic sensors. These are superior to traditional potentiometer-based analog sensors. In addition to being more precise and more sensitive, they have no moving parts that can wear out and are thus naturally resistant to stick drift. 16 total buttons all customizable through the OLED display or GG app The Aeon Pro has a d-pad and twelve programmable buttons, all of which use satisfyingly clicky mechanical switches. These include: four XYAB buttons, four trigger buttons, and four rear paddle switches. Two of the trigger buttons also feature adjustable travel length; with a flick of a switch you can choose either full travel or a hair trigger. The buttons can all be customized using the OLED display on the controller or via the Steelseries GG app. Modular thumbsticks Are you a sucker for interchangeable thumbsticks? The Aeon Pro has got that too. Included in the package are four different styles of modular thumbsticks that you can swap out: convex, concave, standard length, and long. They simply snap onto either joystick position and are a nice touch that you'll only find in premium controllers. It's not cheap, but few great things are. I've seen and tested so many tournament controllers, but none with all the technology that's packed into the Aeon Pro. Yes it's expensive, but if you're a heavy gamer that uses a controller for hundreds of hours, then this is so worth it. items.title: Razer Reveals New Pokémon Gaming Headsets Featuring Sylveon, Charizard, and Lucario
items.content_text: Razer just dropped three new Pokémon-inspired headsets. The new colorways, which form part of Pokémon’s ongoing 30th anniversary celebrations, are for two of the tech company’s most popular gaming headsets: the Kraken V4 and the Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed. In typical collab fashion, each design is based on a specific Pokémon. This particular collection puts the spotlight on Sylveon, Charizard, and Lucario. The headsets are now available directly from Razer and Target, though with a significant markup at the latter. 3 New Razer x Pokémon Gaming Headsets Now Available The Razer Kraken V4 is getting the Sylveon Edition treatment. This wired headset sports a retractable mic, 7.1 surround sound, and customizable RGB with Razer Chroma. The Sylveon design is all about the pastels, with an image of Sylveon printed on the headband and soft blue details on the earcups. Razer’s own official listing calls the new edition “coquette-style.” The base model headset costs $79.99, and the Sylveon Edition is currently listed at Razer for the same price. The Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed headset is getting two new colorways based on some of the coolest Pokemon, Charizard and Lucario. This is a slightly higher-end headset tuned specifically for esports, with the standard edition priced at $20 more than the Kraken V4. It’s also lighter, weighing 270g to the Kraken’s 300g. Razer boasts a low-latency wireless connection supported by 2.4GHz HyperSpeed technology and up to 70 hours of battery life. The Charizard edition is colored in black and red flames with orange lining, while the Lucario model features vibrant blue earcubs and ink-like illustrations. Where to Buy Razer Kraken V4 - Sylveon Edition Razer ($79.99) Target ($109.99) Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed - Lucario Edition Razer ($99.99) Target ($139.99) Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed - Charizard Edition Razer ($99.99) Target ($139.99) Razer has previously released a number of Pokémon-themed peripherals, including a general Pokémon line of accessories and the viral Gengar headset . It’s not surprising to see the two companies lock hands once again for the gaming giant’s 30th anniversary. Meanwhile Target, which is selling the new Razer headsets at a significant markup, released an entire Pokémon anniversary collection earlier this summer.

items.title: Will You Be Taking Time Off Work or School for GTA 6's Release Next Month?
items.excerpt: We are just a little over 30 days until the release of GTA 6, which begs the question: will you be taking time off of work or school to play it?
items.content_text: We are just a little over 30 days away from the release of GTA 6 , which begs the question: Will you be taking time off of work or school to play it? GTA 6 is one of the biggest pop culture events of the decade, if not in all of history, and as a result, it's expected to cause some disruption. In addition to fears that the game's highly-anticipated launch may create instability for ISPs and platform servers, many companies are also expected to have an irregular amount of employees calling out for the day. For months, fans on social media have been claiming they're putting in PTO requests well in advance of November to ensure they can have the game's release weekend available. So, will you be taking November 19 off? Let us know in the poll below, dear reader. Economists have estimated that there will be a $1 billion loss in productivity during launch week due to people being absent from their jobs. A car tuning company known as Burger Motorsports has even announced that it will be closed on November 19 , the day of the game's release, due to an excess of employees requesting that day off. The Australian government has also released some interesting PSAs, informing citizens about their rights when it comes to taking time off around the release of GTA 6 . The U.S. Army even offered soldiers four days of time off for the game's launch if they reenlist . NBA star Steven Adams also joked that the various sports leagues would see a drop in performance due to the release of GTA 6 . Of course, Rockstar is ensuring that, regardless of performance, sports fans are hyper-aware of its upcoming game thanks to an unprecdented GTA 6-themed NBA regular season game in Miami and a blitz of advertising at the Hard Rock Stadium where the Miami Dolphins play . It's likely we will see a slew of other companies joining in on the GTA 6 hype as the game's launch approaches. Rockstar Games is making sure the whole world knows that its highly-anticipated release is nearly here after multiple delays. A plethora of ads have been spotted in and around Miami, New York City, and Paris. Rockstar is also investing a boatload of cash into the game's music, as it has produced an album filled with original music from the likes of Cardi B, Travis Scott, and Keith Richards . The game's radio stations will also be hosted by major musicians like Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, and Bad Bunny, where they will play a variety of mainstream hits. The 13-year wait for a new GTA game is nearly over as GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. A PC version is also rumored to release in the first quarter of 2027 .

items.title: SPECS, Snap's First-Ever AR Glasses, Ships Out This Fall
items.excerpt: A new, lightweight and stylish personal wearable computer.
items.content_text: Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by Snap. Snap Inc., the company behind Snapchat, has opened up preorders for its first ever augmented reality (AR) glasses - SPECS . It's expected to ship out in the United States, United Kingdom, and France sometime in the fall of 2026. Where to Preorder Snap's Upcoming SPECS AR Glasses SPECS is designed to be a pair of glasses that you can wear daily for prolonged periods of time. It's made of a resilient and lightweight Swiss TR90 thermoplastic and comes in two sizes - 47mm and 52mm - with the smaller size weighing in at 4.6 ounces. That's heavier than a standard pair of glasses, but impressive nonetheless considering the fact that SPECS is equipped with advanced optics and a personal wearable computer. The preorder price is set at $2,195, including a $200 refundable deposit to lock in your reservation. SPECS is being marketed as the most advanced consumer AR glasses Instead of an actual powered display, SPECS uses transparent waveguide technology to project UI elements onto seemingly ordinary lenses without compromising your spatial awareness. Alternatively, it can project a full-color immersive display with 51-degree field of view, equivalent to a 115-inch cinema screen placed about ten feet away. The glasses are electrochromatic, meaning they automatically tint based on lighting conditions, and they are prescription compatible. The integrated PC is equipped with dual Snapdragon processors and runs off the proprietary Snap OS 2.0 operating system. Thanks to an array of onboard infared and RGB cameras and sensors, SPECS is able to combine computer vision, contextual awareness, and AI assistance to understand the user's surroundings and deliver relevant information and experiences in real time. Because SPECS is developed by Snap, an established company with years of research poured into augmented reality, it can leverage the company's existing AR ecosystem and Lens platform. SPECS is a tetherless experience with an estimated 4-hour battery life under mixed-use operation. Don't think that's long enough for you? SPECS includes a charging case that can extend your total usage time to 20 hours. Is SPECS for everyone? No, not everyone can spend $2,100 on eyewear . But if you're a creator looking for an innovative way to produce content, a professional seeking spatial productivity tools, a traveler looking for an alternative to traditional screen-based computing, or just someone who's interested in AI-powered wearable technology, the practical benefits (and coolness factor) could be well worth the cost of entry. items.title: I Didn't Want a Greta Gerwig Narnia Movie... Until I Watched the Magician's Nephew Trailer
items.excerpt: We didn't think the world needed a Narnia reboot, at least until the trailer for Greta Gerwig's The Magician's Nephew showed us just how wrong we were.
items.content_text: The first trailer for Netflix’s The Magician’s Nephew has arrived, giving us all a closer look at director Greta Gerwig’s follow-up to 2023’s Barbie. And apart from also being a bold, subversive take on an iconic property, the two movies could scarcely be more different. It’s also clear that Netflix is going in a vastly different direction with the Narnia franchise compared to previous live-action movies. And as far as I’m concerned, that’s fantastic. Before today, I wasn’t particularly enthralled with the idea of Gerwig rebooting Narnia. But having watched the trailer, that iconic Shaquille O’Neal meme comes to mind. I owe you an apology, Greta; I wasn’t really familiar with your game. Mind you, my relative disinterest in Gerwig’s Narnia reboot was never a reflection of the director herself. She’s easily one of the brightest new voices in the film scene today. She’s proven she can handle semi-autobiographical indie comedies like Frances Ha and Lady Bird just as well as she does big-budget blockbusters like Barbie . Like Ryan Coogler, she’s that rare combination of a talented creator with compelling stories to tell and someone who can actually navigate the tumultuous studio system without her voice being drowned out. It’s precisely because Gerwig is such an important voice in the industry that I found the Narnia news a little disappointing. The world is Gerwig’s oyster after the massive success of Barbie. She can pretty much tackle anything she wants. So why reboot the Narnia series of all things? Why tackle another studio project rather than seek out and develop the next Lady Bird? Granted, a big part of my problem here is my own lack of attachment to the Narnia franchise itself. I’ve never been able to connect with Narnia in either book or movie form. It’s just always felt too stuffy and wrapped up in religious allegory for my tastes. Strangely, that’s never stopped me from becoming obsessed with Lev Grossman’s Magicians books, which basically pose the question, “What if you combined Hogwarts and Narnia and populated them with horny young adults?” Having now seen the trailer, it’s obvious that Gerwig does indeed see something powerful in the source material. So I’ll admit my previous disinterest in The Magician’s Nephew is based partly on selfish reasons. I may not have found much to love in these books, but that doesn’t mean the same is true for Gerwig. If she felt compelled to make this her next big film project after Barbie, clearly there was a reason for that. And having now seen the trailer, it’s obvious that Gerwig does indeed see something powerful in the source material. The trailer makes a huge, bold statement. It immediately establishes just how different this reboot is from any Narnia project that’s come before. It immediately cuts to the heart of what I think is the fundamental appeal of Narnia (and The Magicians, for that matter) - that desire for ordinary youngsters to escape their humdrum world and find something better on the other side. Visually, the trailer is a real feast for the eyes. There’s color galore, and no shortage of psychedelic fantasy imagery. The whole thing looks very much like a trippy painting someone would have slapped on the side of a dilapidated van in 1978. It’s just f***ing cool in a way I never would have associated with the Narnia franchise. I immediately want to see this movie, regardless of whatever 100-year-old fantasy franchise it may or may not be associated with. And you can’t discount the power of a good Led Zeppelin tune. As we saw from past trailers like 2011’s The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo and 2017’s Thor: Ragnarok, blasting out Zeppelin on top of a frenetic montage of imagery is like a cheat code to win over jaded middle-aged moviegoers like myself. Plus, you have to enjoy the irony of having the notoriously Lord of the Rings-obsessed rock band serving as the soundtrack for a Narnia movie instead. I fully suspect some hardcore Narnia lovers will take umbrage at the trailer. It’s clear that Gerwig isn’t opting for a 100% book-faithful adaptation here. But that’s exactly why I‘m so intrigued by what we’re seeing. Gerwig is forgoing strict accuracy in favor of building a take that speaks to her and her particular sensibilities. It seems likely she’s taking the opportunity to use this franchise to tell a very Greta Gerwig-type story, just as she did with Barbie and Little Women in years past. Before today, I didn’t particularly want a new Narnia movie. But the trailer is proof of just how wrong and misguided I was. This film has gone from being barely a blip on my radar to one of my most anticipated films of 2027. Kudos, Ms. Gerwig. Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. items.content_text: Official K/DA accounts have been updated for the first time in six years. New profile and banner images continue to show the existing promotional art from the All Out era, now with the addition of hot pink flames. The reactivated accounts have also wiped existing posts, fueling rumors that the virtual girl group is gearing up for a comeback. K/DA, which debuted at the 2018 League of Legends World Championship, consists of four League champions (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'Sa) voiced by international pop stars. The group’s first single, aptly called POP/STARS, was the first K-pop song by a girl group to receive RIAA Platinum certification in 2022. The early success of the girl group prompted the release of a full EP, All Out, in 2020. Since then, the group has pretty much gone dark. K/DA skins still exist in-game, but there’s been no word on new music or performances. Until now. I’m not asking for much. I just want to see a teaser from K/DA that’s as peak as this. https://t.co/gWU9yf04w9 — RainySeason (@CookieNevie) October 13, 2026 An updated banner image continues to use promotional images from the All Out era, showing the main K/DA quartet alongside the era’s guest artist, Seraphine, who was a newly released champion at the time. As of October 13, however, those images also show the addition of hot pink and magenta flames. Datamined leaks from earlier this year already raised hopes that the group would have some role in the current season of League of Legends. Details in a Wild Rift update, first spotted by SkinSpotlights , pointed to a potential “Firestarter” skin concept, as well as a new song registered on the ASCAP Repertory. That being said, I'm not exactly a Fallout superfan with tons of disposable income, so I'm likely not the target market for such a product. items.title: Xbox Announces Xbox Labs, Aimed in Part at Getting Improved Old-Gen Games Playable in Web Browsers
items.excerpt: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.
items.content_text: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers. No doubt seeing the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved), Microsoft itself is keen to get in on the action in support of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goal of reaching 1 billion players per day . Xbox has been tinkering with running Xbox and Xbox 360 games in browsers, and the Xbox Labs initiative is a formalization of those efforts that will see a small team of engineers playing with emerging technologies in order to find new ways for games new and old to be distributed and even created. And IGN understands that this won't just be an R&D effort; rather, Xbox Labs is tasked with shipping products – Sharma says, "We'll build in the open" – and getting gamers to engage with them. I'd suggest thinking about it as a next phase of the backward compatibility efforts that started at Xbox over a decade ago, which the recent disc-to-digital program built on (which, side note, is a much more consumer-friendly path towards the seemingly inevitable digital future than what Sony is doing ), and now Xbox Labs aims to take it even further. It remains to be seen if or how Xbox will look to monetize its Xbox Labs offerings, be it via an upfront cost, in-game microtransactions, or in-game-ad-based revenue . The Xbox Labs announcement continues a busy stretch for Xbox, which revealed its entertainment-industry-focused Xbox XP arm last week. Here's Sharma's memo to the team (also posted to Xbox Wire ) in full: Team, The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together. In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another. These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating. I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have. Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway. Asha

items.title: The Best Street Fighter Anime You've Never Seen
items.excerpt: The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it?
items.content_text: The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it? Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie came out in 1994, the same year that the so-bad-it's-good live-action film with Jean-Claude Van Damme and Raul Julia was released. And while the highly-quotable (“For me, it was Tuesday”) live-action flick is a larger part of the public consciousness, most Street Fighter fans will agree that the animated movie blows it out of the water. The animated movie doesn’t follow the World Warrior tournament seen in the game; instead, it focuses on Bison tracking down strong warriors using an army of cyborgs in an attempt to capture them for his own nefarious purposes. It’s not an official part of the official Street Fighter lore (which, admittedly, is quite confusing and convoluted), but it features some fantastic fights and, of course, the debut of Violent Ken (an evil version of the character corrupted by M. Bison's Psycho Power). You’ve likely seen some GIFs from this movie floating around the internet over the years, and that’s no coincidence. The animation in this flick is simply fantastic, especially where fight scenes are concerned. One of the first ones we see takes place between Ryu and Sagat as a little backstory (which actually is canon); other iconic action sequences include Cammy’s assassination of a government official, Ryu and Ken’s final fight against M. Bison, and of course, Chun-Li’s iconic brawl with Vega. Fights aside, one of the reasons the animated movie is so deeply beloved by fans is that it stays true to Street Fighter’s colorful cast of characters. Just like in the games, Ryu is a deeply contemplative, compassionate man on a perpetual journey of self-improvement; Ken is decidedly more hot-headed but maintains an aura of discipline learned from master Gouken; Guile is a classic American military man whose stoic facade breaks into goofy moments now and then; Chun-Li is a badass kung-fu practitioner who manages to keep hold of her girlish, quirky side; and Bison is a menacing, gangster overlord whose Psycho Power makes him feel like a serious threat. Given it was the '90s, this version of Street Fighter doesn’t shy away from blood and nudity. In fact, there’s a fairly gratuitous shower scene that highlights Chun-Li’s physique, directly after which she tousles with Vega in a brutal, bloody battle. It’s not a family-friendly film, but it’s possibly the most accurate depiction of what the Street Fighter universe would actually be like if psycho-powered dictators and super-powered martial artists actually roamed the world. Since it's an animated movie, it's also easier to sell the believability of its overall premise. Live-action adaptations have the challenge of making larger-than-life moves like E. Honda's Sumo Headbutt or Chun-Li's Spinning Bird Kick look realistic enough to fit into the real world; animated movies have the luxury of getting to bypass this, giving artists far more creative freedom in translating these moments from concept to page. This is one of the key reasons why the Street Fighter II animated movie pulls things off so well, and it set the standard for other adaptations in the years to come. It'd be remiss not to mention the other animated Street Fighter films and series that exist, as well. The Street Fighter Alpha animated movie is a visual spectacle that unfortunately falls flat where story is concerned; the Street Fighter II V anime series is painful to watch, and we won't even get into the mess that was the American cartoon (though it also has some pretty quotable moments). It's clear, though, that the 1994 animated movie is the one to watch out of the lot, and as a diehard Street Fighter fan, I'd argue that it's required viewing if you're trying to get into the franchise. Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie is available to watch on Crunchyroll, Pluto TV, and Amazon Prime Video at the time of writing this piece. It’s absolutely worth viewing, especially if you’re wanting to learn more about the world of the games ahead of the 2026 movie (or if you just want some badass anime fights). If you’re keen on diving into the games, you can check out our breakdown of how to play each of them in chronological order , or read our article diving into the nearly forty-year-old history of this iconic fighting game franchise from beginning to end.

items.title: Save an Extra 10% Off Alienware's Budget Friendly 27" QD-OLED Gaming Monitor With 240Hz Refresh Rate
items.excerpt: Buy two and create a massive 49" 5120x1440 multi-monitor setup for an affordable price.
items.content_text: Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. They're also really expensive. Well, Alienware is bucking the trend with one of its latest 2026 OLED releases. The 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor is listed at an already reasonable price of $349.99, but right now there's a 10% off discount that drops it to $314.99 with free shipping. It comes with the same three year warranty with OLED burn-in coverage you would get with Alienware's other pricier monitors. Extra 10% Off 27" Alienware AW2726DM OLED Gaming Monitor The Alienware AW2726DM is a 27" monitor with a 2560x1440 resolution and a pixel density of 111ppi, which is sharp enough for both gaming and general workstation use and boasts excellent text clarity. The panel uses Samsung's quantum dot OLED technology. A QD OLED panel is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more commonly found W-OLED panel. OLED monitors in general offer superior image quality compared to other monitors thanks to a combination of instantaneous response time, near-infinite black levels, and near-infinite contrast ratio. Most "budget" OLED monitors have a native 60Hz-144Hz refresh rate, but the AW2726DM ups the ante with a native 240Hz panel, making it a great choice for games that have high-speed motion or require twitch-like reflexes (for example sports games, racing sims, and first person shooters). You'll need to make sure you have an appropriate graphics card to achieve 240fps on a QHD monitor, ideally something like an RTX 5070 Ti or Radeon RX 9070 XT , although an RTX 5070 will be fine for older games like The Witcher 3, Fortnite, Apex Legends, Counter-Strike, or Valorant. Two of these monitors would make a great multi-monitor setup for the upcoming Forza Horizon 6 game . Two of these monitors side-by-side is equivalent to a 49" monitor with 5120x1440 resolution and it will be a lot cheaper than buying a dedicated 49" OLED monitor with similar specs. Finally, the AW2726DM does include a 3 year warranty that includes burn-in coverage, which most other brands do not offer. Burn-in is less of an issue than it used to be because there are built-in, automated features designed to prevent it, but it can still happen. Dell offers assurance that it will address the issue if it ever arises. items.title: EA Sports' College Football Devs Reportedly Fear the Franchise Could Disappear by 2030
items.excerpt: Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade.
items.content_text: Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade. The report comes from Insider Gaming's Mike Straw , who spoke to senior-level sources working on or around the football series. He noted that, although the series is performing well, sales have gradually declined entry to entry since its highly-anticipated debut in 2024. While this isn't inherently a bad thing (or unexpected, given the extreme hype around the 2024 title), costs associated with the game have been rising. Per the report, in 2024, EA paid each player featured in the game $600, amounting to roughly $7 million total. Those costs have tripled, with NIL (name, image, likeness) rights for college athletes now costing $1,500 per player. As a result, EA spent roughly $20 million on its players with its latest game. EA also pays boatloads of cash to license bowl games, universities, and more, meaning tens of millions of dollars goes into just having the right to use certain elements in the game as opposed to raw development costs. This has led to EA trying to monetize key areas of the game, including College Football's single-player modes. This led to extreme backlash earlier this summer due to the fact players felt they were being pushed to pay to efficently play single-player content. EA eventually bent the knee and reversed course , but noted that it would retool these options and bring them back in future entries. One source told Insider Gaming that microtransactions were planned to return in future College Football single-player titles, and feared that it would anger players, pushing them away from a game that is trying to grow. While there are College Football games planned for the next few years, sources reportedly fear that the franchise may be on its way out. "We’re not FC. We’re not Madden. We don’t make the money they do, and everyone knows it," a source told Insider Gaming. "But it’s at the point where if we don’t find a way to keep players around and, in turn, make more, we won’t have anything. Forget in 10 years, I’m scared about if we have a game by the end of the decade. Games aren’t getting cheaper to make, and there’s the real concern with all of us that EA’s going to streamline and just have a few key franchises and dump everything else." Insider Gaming noted that not all of its sources shared these fears and some believed there is a strong future with the franchise. EA Sports' College Football brand is a spiritual successor to EA Sports' highly popular NCAA football series that thrived in the 2000s and early 2010s before legal issues surrounding NIL rights effectively killed it. There was a 14-year gap between NCAA's final game and the debut of the new College Football series, which led to an extreme level of enthusiasm from fans. It led to College Football 25 raking in big bucks and becoming the second best selling game of 2024 in the United States, though it hasn't sustained that momentum year-to-year. College Football 26 was the seventh best selling game in the United States in 2025, with College Football 27 currently placed in 10th this year. Of course, College Football also doesn't have as much global appeal as something like EA's FC series, which means its sales are primarily made up in the US.
